subject: Clarify long-context billing and minimum floor for Acme pilot
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: J. Miller <jmiller@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify long-context billing and minimum floor for Acme pilot

Marcus —

Thanks for the call earlier. Three quick questions that came up internally as we try to finalize the pilot economics:

1) Long-context sessions: many of our agents will reference a running doc history (12–40k tokens typical; occasional bursts to 80k). How is that charged under the "minimum floor" rules? Do you charge the full token delta for the entire context every request, or does Redwood apply prefix/KV caching credits to avoid double-charging repeated context?

2) Sliding/deferred minimums: Our PSD suggests a day-level or week-level smoothing window (we don't want to pay a large micro-floor on low-traffic days). Can Redwood do a rolling floor (e.g., 7-day average) or is the floor strictly per-invoice period?

3) Discount triggers: we need to decide how the long-context tier affects committed discounts. If we commit to N tokens/month but 40% of those tokens are long-context KV replay, how does that influence the tier calculation?

We're trying to map to a real invoice example — attaching a small anonymized usage snapshot from this week. Can you propose a couple options (one conservative, one customer-friendly) for the pilot?

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Head of Product
Acme AI

Attachments: acme_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify long-context billing and minimum floor for Acme pilot

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear framing. Short answers up front, then a couple of concrete proposals with worked examples.

Quick summary:
- We bill for tokens consumed by the request (prompt + response) after de-duplication: if the same prefix is reused and served from KV cache, it is not re-billed per-token — instead you get KV-cache credits that offset charges. However, very long first-time context ingestion is billed.
- Floor application: floors are applied at invoice-level by default, but we can offer a rolling smoothing window for pilots (7- or 30-day average) as an addendum to the contract.
- Discount triggers: committed volume tiers are based on billable tokens after KV-cache credits; for negotiations we can show both gross and net token outlines so you can see the delta.

Proposal A — conservative (standard floor semantics)
- Pilot commit: 300M billable tokens / month for 6 months
- Minimum floor: invoice-level monthly floor of 3M billable tokens (applies after caching credits)
- Discount: 15% off list for committed tier; overage billed at list minus 5% pilot uplift
- Pros: predictable for Redwood; easy to model

Example: if your gross context ingestion is 400M tokens but 120M are served entirely from KV cache during the month, billable tokens = 280M; invoice-floor doesn't kick in. If billable tokens fall to 2.4M in a low week, monthly floor still enforces 3M.

Proposal B — customer-friendly (adaptive floor + smoothing)
- Pilot commit: 250M billable tokens / month for 6 months
- Adaptive floor: daily floor of 0.1x (10%) of committed monthly projected tokens averaged over most recent 7 days; floors are evaluated weekly so big microbursts don't permanently charge you for a single low-traffic day
- Smoothing credit: we apply a 7-day rolling offset so days below threshold borrow from preceding days' excess billable usage
- Discount: 20% off list if commit >= 6 months and agree to a usage review at 3 months

Worked example (adaptive): committed 250M/month => daily nominal target ~8.3M. 10% floor => daily floor ~830k, evaluated as 7-day rolling average. If you have three heavy days (40M total) and four light days (<200k/day), the rolling logic smooths the invoice-level impact.

Operational notes:
- We will expose per-request "cache-hit" metadata in the Console so you can independently validate KV credits.
- For long ingest operations (one-time multi-100k token uploads), we recommend using the batch-ingest API which is priced differently and can be flagged as "non-billable trial ingestion" for pilot customers if agreed up front.

Next steps I propose:
- I can send a short addendum with the adaptive floor language and an example invoice layout.
- We'll attach a sample invoice and a pricing-deck that maps your usage snapshot into both proposals.

Cc'ing Kimberly for contract language and Aditya for the pilot billing sample. We'll also drop a short spreadsheet with scenario calculations.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-deck.pdf (12 slides), pricing-scenarios.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

From: J. Miller <jmiller@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify long-context billing and minimum floor for Acme pilot

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement's immediate asks: 

1) We need explicit contract language that defines: 
   - "KV-cache credit" and how it's calculated (example formula requested).
   - The rolling-floor algorithm (we prefer a deterministic formula we can test against historical data).
2) Please provide a sample invoice for both Proposal A and B for our accounting team.
3) SOW: we have internal legal constraints that require the pilot SOW to show any "non-billable ingestion" items and who owns the data during that window.

If you can surface a DocuSign-ready SOW + a sample invoice by end of day Monday (29th) we can review with legal and come back with redlines.

Also: can you include an example amendment clause that caps our liability for overages during the pilot period while the rolling smoothing is being tuned?

Thanks — J. Miller (on behalf of Procurement)
Attachments: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: J. Miller <jmiller@acme.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify long-context billing and minimum floor for Acme pilot

J. / Priya —

Good — we'll turn around the materials you requested. Action items from our side: 

- Kimberly will draft the amendment language that: 

  (a) defines KV-cache-credit = gross_ingested_prompt_tokens * cache_hit_rate_adjustment (we'll supply a deterministic formula + two worked examples);
  (b) specifies the rolling-floor: 7-day simple moving average on billable tokens with a weekly reconciliation window.
- Aditya will produce two sample invoices (Proposal A / Proposal B) using your attached usage snapshot and the spreadsheet we sent.
- I'll prepare the SOW addendum identifying non-billable ingestion (batch-ingest marked as trial ingestion) and a proposed DocuSign SOW link.

Deliverables & ETA:
- Draft amendment + sample invoice PDFs: Monday 2026-11-29 EOD PT
- DocuSign-ready SOW (template) for review: Monday 2026-11-29 EOD PT
- Internal sync (30 min) to review prior to your legal call: Tuesday 2026-11-30 09:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite if that works.

Sample invoice snippet (illustrative)
- Proposal B (Adaptive) — November sample month
  Gross token ingestion: 412,324,589
  KV cache credits applied: -124,100,000
  Net billable tokens: 288,224,589
  Committed monthly floor (7-day adaptive eval): equivalent to 7-day SMA floor => 5,810,000 (applied as smoothing credit where needed)
  Discount (20% pilot): -57,644,918 tokens equivalent credit
  Billable tokens invoiced: 230,579,671

I'll attach the two invoice PDFs and the redwood-pricing-deck to the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Marcus Lin
